blueprint.name: Register an existing IBM ROKS cluster (no BNK install)
blueprint.description: Adopt a ROKS cluster you already own into a roksbnkctl workspace and register it with BNK Forge — and stop there. Nothing is created, nothing is installed: the cluster, its VPC and its worker pool are left exactly as found, and BNK is never touched. Use it to bring a cluster under management so it is visible on the Kubernetes page, to fetch a kubeconfig into a shared deployment workspace, or to attach the cluster's VPC to a Transit Gateway ahead of a disconnected install. The BNK install blueprints do this same registration as their first step, so this is that step on its own.

outcomes: An existing ROKS cluster adopted into the workspace (cluster-outputs.json)
The cluster registered with BNK Forge and visible on the Kubernetes page
A kubeconfig fetched into the shared deployment workspace
Optionally, the cluster's VPC attached to an existing Transit Gateway

prerequisites.description: An IBM Cloud credential template on the project. Region and resource group inherit from it.
A ROKS cluster that already exists in the named region and resource group. It is adopted, never created.

input_summary.label: What it changes
input_summary.value: Nothing on the cluster. It reads the cluster's identity, writes cluster-outputs.json and a kubeconfig into the deployment workspace, registers the cluster with Forge, and — only if you name a gateway — attaches the cluster's VPC to it.

input_summary.label: BNK is not installed
input_summary.value: This blueprint carries no bnk-install module. To install BNK onto the cluster, use 'BNK on an existing IBM ROKS cluster' (connected) or 'BNK on a disconnected IBM ROKS cluster' (air-gapped) — both perform this registration themselves as their first step, so you do not need to run this one first.

input_summary.label: Teardown
input_summary.value: Destroy runs `bnkforge unregister` then `tgw disconnect --auto`. It never runs `cluster down`: the cluster survives, because this blueprint never created it. A Transit Gateway attachment that pre-existed is left alone — roksbnkctl records it without managing it.

input_summary.label: One cluster, one project
input_summary.value: Since roksbnkctl v1.42.0 `bnkforge register` REFUSES a cluster already held by another Forge project rather than silently moving it. Release the other project's registration first if you mean to re-home the cluster.

required.name: prefix
required.label: Resource prefix
required.description: Prefix roksbnkctl uses for anything it names in the workspace. It does NOT rename the cluster — the cluster is identified by 'Existing cluster name' below.

required.name: cluster_name
required.label: Existing cluster name (or id)
required.description: Name or id of the ROKS cluster to adopt. It must already exist in the region and resource group below. It is never created and never destroyed by this blueprint.

required.name: region
required.label: IBM Cloud region
required.description: Region the cluster lives in. Inherits from the selected credential template. A mismatch surfaces later as a confusing 'cluster not found' for a cluster you can plainly see in the console.

required.name: resource_group
required.label: Resource group
required.description: IBM Cloud resource group the cluster is in. Inherits from the selected credential template.

optional.name: existing_transit_gateway
optional.label: Existing Transit Gateway (name or id)
optional.description: Attach the cluster's VPC to this gateway as part of the registration. Leave blank to register the cluster and touch its networking not at all — which is the right answer for a connected cluster, and for one whose VPC is already attached. Supply it when you are preparing the cluster for a disconnected install and it must reach a private registry and License Proxy over the gateway. An attachment that already exists is adopted, not re-created.

optional.name: registry_cos_name
optional.label: Registry COS instance name
optional.description: Overrides the registry COS instance `cluster register` looks for. Blank = probe <prefix>-registry-cos, <cluster>-registry-cos, <cluster>-cos.

optional.name: cos_instance
optional.label: Supply-chain COS instance
optional.description: COS instance holding the FAR auth key + subscription JWT. Blank = bnk-supply-chain. Registration itself needs no entitlement material; this only matters if a later module reuses this workspace.

optional.name: cos_bucket
optional.label: Supply-chain COS bucket
optional.description: Bucket holding the FAR auth key + subscription JWT. Blank = bnk-artifacts. Account-suffixed buckets (bnk-artifacts-<account>) must be named explicitly. Only matters if a later module reuses this workspace.

optional.name: cos_region
optional.label: Supply-chain COS region
optional.description: Region of that bucket. Blank = us-south.

optional.name: far_auth_file
optional.label: FAR auth object name
optional.description: Object name of the FAR auth tarball in the bucket. Blank = f5-far-auth-key.tgz.

optional.name: subscription_jwt_file
optional.label: Subscription JWT object name
optional.description: Object name of the subscription JWT in the bucket. Blank = subscription.jwt.

optional.name: manifest_version
optional.label: BNK manifest version
optional.description: BNK manifest release the workspace is pinned to. Blank = the roksbnkctl default. Registration does not read it; it is recorded for a later install that shares this workspace.

optional.name: bnkforge_url
optional.label: BNK Forge URL
optional.description: Forge to register the cluster into. Blank skips the Forge registration entirely and leaves you with the workspace adoption only.

optional.name: bnkforge_username
optional.label: BNK Forge username
optional.description: Username used to register the cluster.

optional.name: bnkforge_password
optional.label: BNK Forge password
optional.description: Password for that login. Passed to the step as an environment variable only — never on the command line.

optional.name: bnkforge_project
optional.label: BNK Forge project
optional.description: Project to register the cluster into. Blank = this project.

optional.name: bnkforge_insecure
optional.label: Skip Forge TLS verification
optional.description: Set true only for a Forge with a self-signed certificate. Defaults to false — verification stays on unless you opt out.

optional.name: ibmcloud_api_key
optional.label: IBM Cloud API key
optional.description: Filled from the project's credential template at creation and carried by the module, so it keeps working even if the project's template is cleared later.

optional.name: bnkforge_ca_b64
optional.label: BNK Forge CA (base64 PEM)
optional.description: Base64 PEM of the CA that issued the Forge server's certificate, pinning the registration call. Supply this INSTEAD of 'Skip Forge TLS verification': roksbnkctl v1.50.0 warns on every unverified Forge request, and a pin answers that warning rather than silencing it. Blank when the certificate is publicly trusted.

modules.name: roksbnkctl Cluster Registry
modules.description: init -> cluster register -> kubeconfig fetch -> bnkforge register, against a cluster that already exists. Creates no infrastructure.
